title: `seekable(..., maxlen=0)` loses items on `peek()` and `bool()`
spec:
This is the more-itertools library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 run_tests.py`.

With `maxlen=0` (no history kept), peeking or truth-testing a `seekable` consumes items, so they never come out of the iterator:

```python
import more_itertools as mi
s = mi.seekable([10, 20, 30], maxlen=0)
s.peek(), s.peek()   # expected (10, 10), actual (10, 20)
list(s)              # expected [10, 20, 30], actual [30]
```

Likewise `s = mi.seekable([10, 20, 30], maxlen=0); bool(s)` is `True` as expected, but `list(s)` is then `[20, 30]` instead of `[10, 20, 30]`. `bool(mi.seekable([], maxlen=0))` should still be `False`.

`peek()` and `bool()` are documented as looking ahead without advancing; that should hold for every `maxlen`, including 0.
acceptance: Repeated `peek()` on a `maxlen=0` seekable returns the same item and nothing is lost
`bool()` on a `maxlen=0` seekable does not consume an item, and is False when empty
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
